title: Implement wildcard pattern matching where '?' matches any single character and '*' matches any sequence of characters including the empty sequence.

s1_definition.oneliner: Star absorbs one more text char (cell above) or matches empty (cell left); question mark or exact char matches via the diagonal.
s1_definition.profdef:
Wildcard Matching uses 2D DP where dp[i][j] means the first i text chars match the first j pattern chars.

- **Star** is standalone: it matches any sequence including empty. dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] (absorb one more) OR dp[i][j-1] (match empty).
- **Question mark** or exact character match requires dp[i-1][j-1] when the single char matches.
- **First row** is true across a leading run of stars because each star can match empty.
- **Time** is O(m * n) and **space** reducible to O(n).
- **Greedy alternative** with a saved star position solves in O(m * n) worst case but O(1) space.
s1_definition.analogy: A file-name matcher at National Bank of India filters statement files by a glob pattern. A question mark matches exactly one character and a star matches any run of characters. At a star the matcher can either swallow one more character or declare the star finished.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  DP Table for s="adceb", p="*a*b":

       ""  *  a  *  b
  ""  [ T  T  F  F  F ]
  a   [ F  T  T  T  F ]
  d   [ F  T  F  T  F ]
  c   [ F  T  F  T  F ]
  e   [ F  T  F  T  F ]
  b   [ F  T  F  T  T ]

  Star Logic (standalone):
  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
  │ dp[i][j] for * at position j:    │
  │                                  │
  │ dp[i-1][j]:  absorb one char     │
  │              (star keeps going)   │
  │              ↑ from cell above    │
  │                                  │
  │ dp[i][j-1]:  match empty          │
  │              (star is done)       │
  │              ← from cell left     │
  └─────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Wildcard Matching is a 2D DP problem that is simpler than Regex Matching because the star here is standalone and matches any sequence directly, rather than being tied to a preceding element. I define dp[i][j] as whether the first i characters of the text match the first j characters of the pattern. The star has two branches: absorb one more text character (cell above) or match empty (cell left). A question mark or exact character match inherits the diagonal.

The first row is true across a leading run of stars because each star can match the empty text. The body fills left to right, top to bottom, and the answer is the bottom-right cell. Space reduces to O(n) with rolling arrays.

At National Bank of India, a batch processor filtered statement file names by a glob pattern where a question mark matched one character and a star matched any run. Because a star can match nothing or a long stretch, a plain scan cannot decide where it should stop, which is why DP is needed.

The greedy two-pointer variant with a saved star position is a strong follow-up that achieves the same worst-case time with O(1) space. Explaining both approaches shows the interviewer you understand the tradeoff between clarity and space.

Remember one sentence: star absorbs one more char from above or matches empty from the left, and question mark or exact char matches via the diagonal.

---

keyPoints: dp[i][j] is true when the first i text chars match the first j pattern chars
Star is standalone: dp[i-1][j] absorbs one more char, dp[i][j-1] matches empty
Question mark or exact char match requires dp[i-1][j-1] when the single char matches
The first row is true across leading stars because each star can match empty text
Simpler than Regex Matching because star is not tied to a preceding element
